title: Fold canonical duplicate-axis validation into the axis pass
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: TensorView already visits every retained TensorAxis to validate record type and canonical name ordering, but canonical input then paid a second full adjacent-axis pass solely to reject duplicate names. The same validated axis.name was also read again within the first pass. Because a sorted canonical axis sequence can only contain duplicates adjacently, uniqueness can be checked while the canonical-order pass is already in flight; only a genuinely non-canonical sequence needs the post-sort duplicate check.
primary_claim: Canonical TensorView axis construction now reads each validated axis name once and folds adjacent duplicate-name refusal into the same ordering pass. Non-canonical axes still use the existing sort fallback and post-sort duplicate refusal. Axis ordering, labels, sparse entries, selectors, index projection, wire serialization, digest identity, Fourfold/Forest source binding, status and provenance semantics remain unchanged.
gardener_decision: Delete the redundant canonical-axis uniqueness traversal rather than add an axis index or cache. Reuse the axis name already read for ordering, reject adjacent duplicates in that same pass, and retain the existing sorted fallback only for genuinely non-canonical input. Do not introduce a mapping view, cache, lookup service, alternate Tensor type, planner, store, registry, scheduler or backend.
acceptance: canonical TensorView construction reads every already validated axis name exactly once during axis ordering/uniqueness validation
canonical duplicate axis names still fail closed
non-canonical axes still sort deterministically and duplicate names remain rejected after sorting
